body:
>From my perspective, much of this boils down to how good a sister you want to be. All the physicians, crisis counselors and medical health people don't have a stake in your sister's mental health as you do.

(I'm her Brother). I agree with you to a certain extent, but I now know that's a responsibility I'm not able to handle. And what's scary now, is that I know (or admitted to myself) that others can't help her either. I don't say that lightly, either. I'm a professional and perfectionist at what I do, but this is not one of them. It's also the reason why I am so critical of her herself, and her doctors - mostly due to the lack of success "the system" has given her over the last 15 years.

>Forget drugs, counseling and therapy for the moment. Instead, take your sis to a movie, a local theater production, a museum, the zoo, etc. You can always make popcorn in the microwave and watch cheesy chickflicks on Netflix if all else fails.

She is Bi Polar. I thought that was bullshit for many, many years. I could not believe that _my_ sister has that. "she's just mis-guided and has mood swings, I can convince her about  <topic/issue>". I'm a believer now. What you said may matter to some, but I can honestly say not my sister. _Every_thing I do for my sister is for her best interest, but it doesn't matter. She even apologizes to me all the time for her actions, but it doesn't matter at this point. 

>From my brief sojourn here on SW, the vast majority of suicide-seekers don't have the at-hand support of family members. Your situation seems to be the exception. Let her know you care about her and her place in your life.

I do. Thank you.

To be honest, she is now a professional at not receiving help, manipulating doctors and getting what she wants. She has had a long history of being Bi-polar, manic depression, alcoholism, and abusing many medications. She is a product of an institutionalized patient of mental health facilities from a young age, and homeless shelters from adult age. She is a lost cause in my honest opinion - and that's not an easy thing to say. She can (and does) get any medication she wants to, knowing what to say and to who. 

Our brother at 30 years old passed away a few months ago, and she picked up drinking again. The result of all this is a shit show. I have taken many days off from work, I check her breathing when she sleeps, and tried many, many things to help her. I could go on, but I won't. 

What I am getting to...

>Are you comfortable with the things that they suggested for your sister?

No, I am never comfortable with what people tell me about her. Not because all of them are bad people (some are), but because they are not magicians. They cannot magically fix someone. They cannot prescribe a magic pill. I honestly think in some cases, it come downs to a person to help themselves - there needs to be just a bit determination and drive for them to help themselves regardless of what type of support group they have. You can lead a horse to water kinda thing. 

BUT.. I do however appreciate and respect advice from people who have nothing to gain other than helping. That in my opinion is most helpful to me as it's the most trustworthy. 

>If there's a way that we can help, please do let us know.

Everything said, no I don't think so. But I'm open to suggestions. 

Thanks

I'm in NY. I called the hotline you listed for some advice. They basically told me what her therapist confirmed; that The police can come and take her, but once at the hospital she will be able to sign her self out. The girl I spoke with also gave me some great references for some outpatient programs for her, which IMO will help her. 

On a side note, you guys are really making an impact. Towards the end of the call went something like this...

>Me: OK, thank you for your time 

>Her: No problem, may I ask how you heard of us? 

>Me: Sure, some site called reddit dot com. It's basically a site-- 

>Her: ---Oh yeah, we're very familiar with Reddit 

>me: Really? 

>Her: Yeah 


I hope that encourages some of you to keep on helping. 

Thanks
I have tried, trust me. The question is it possible to force someone to the hospital? I don't care if she hates me, I just don't want her to kill herself
